chunks: Ali ibn Hatim al-Qazwini (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Nahwi narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to us from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abu Ayyub Sulayman ibn Muqbil al-Madini, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), that he said:

When a believer dies, seventy thousand angels attend his funeral until he reaches his grave. When he enters his grave, Munkar and Nakir come to him, seat him, and say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" He says: "My Lord is God, Muhammad is my prophet, and Islam is my religion." Then they expand his grave as far as his eye can see, bring him food from Paradise, and let comfort and relief enter upon him. That is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "And if he was of those brought near, then comfort and relief" -- meaning in his grave -- "and a Garden of Bliss" -- meaning in the Hereafter.

Then he (peace be upon him) said: When a disbeliever dies, seventy thousand angels of punishment attend his funeral until he reaches his grave. He cries out to his carriers in a voice heard by everything except humans and jinn, saying: "If only I had another chance, I would be of the believers," and saying: "Return me, so that I may do righteous deeds in what I left behind." The angels of punishment reply to him: "No! It is merely a word you are saying." An angel calls out to them: "Were he returned, he would go back to what was forbidden to him."

When he enters his grave and the people leave him, Munkar and Nakir come to him in the most horrifying form and stand him up. Then they say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" His tongue trembles and he cannot answer. They strike him with a blow from the chastisement of God, by which all things are terrified. Then they say to him: "Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?" He says: "I do not know." They say to him: "You did not seek knowledge, nor were you guided, nor did you triumph."

Then they open a gate to the Fire for him and bring down to him boiling water from Hell. That is the saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: "But if he was of the denying and astray, then a welcome of boiling water" -- meaning in the grave -- "and burning in Hell" -- meaning in the Hereafter.

key_terms.الثقلان: The Two Weights (humans and jinn), referring to the two categories of beings with moral responsibility
key_terms.الحميم: Boiling water, one of the punishments of Hell
key_terms.الروح والريحان: Comfort and relief/fragrance, blessings given to the righteous in the grave
key_terms.الزبانية: The Zabaniyah, angels of punishment who guard Hell
key_terms.منكر ونكير: Munkar and Nakir, the two angels who question the deceased in the grave

ai.seo_question: What happens to the believer and the disbeliever in the grave according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the contrasting experiences of the believer and the disbeliever in the grave (barzakh). The believer answers the three questions of the grave correctly and is rewarded with expansion of his grave, food from Paradise, and divine comfort, while the disbeliever -- despite pleading for another chance -- fails to answer, is struck with divine punishment, and receives boiling water from Hell. The Imam cites Quran 56:88-89 and 56:92-94 to support these descriptions, interpreting 'comfort and relief' and 'boiling water' as referring to the state of the grave.
